[ASSISTANT_SAID] Being too tolerant can lead to a lack of assertiveness, difficulty making decisions, and feelings of resentment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To reconcile moral priorities with tolerance limits, one should reflect on their values, communicate them clearly, and prioritize their well-being.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To practice being more assertive and setting boundaries, one should identify personal values and limits, start with small steps, use "I" statements, practice saying "no," and seek support.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Building self-confidence can be achieved through self-compassion, challenging negative self-talk, setting achievable goals, taking care of oneself, and surrounding oneself with supportive people.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To stop comparing oneself to others, one should focus on their strengths, practice gratitude, limit social media use, embrace uniqueness, and surround themselves with positive influences.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Gratitude practices include gratitude journaling, gratitude meditation, writing gratitude letters, and creating a gratitude jar.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Gratitude journaling involves writing down a few things one is grateful for each day, being specific and focusing on small joys.  
[USER] The user plans to start practicing saying "no" more often.  
[USER] The user plans to start with gratitude journaling as a practice.
